paper.authors: Waisberg, I.; Klein, Y.; Katz, B.

publication_status.evidence: Crossref 10.33232/001c.138625 (api.crossref.org, checked 2026-10-14): The Open Journal of Astrophysics vol 8, 2025-05-27. Numbers transcribed from the arXiv v2 PDF (2025-05-25) and checked against it table by table.

source_of_data: ESO Phase 3 public GRAVITY products (SINGLE_SCI_VIS, not calibrated), ~/data/eso_binaries/trackb/eta_oph/oifits/; programmes 111.24UP.003, 113.26HF.001. Not an OiDB collection (see DATA_ATTRIBUTION.md, ESO Phase 3).
method: Single-field GRAVITY on the four ATs (K band, science channel, fringe tracker). The authors fit squared visibilities and closure phases with the interferometric binary model of Waisberg+2023 (Sect. 2.2). Free: K flux ratio and (dRA,dDec) per epoch. Diameters of both components fitted in the two longest-baseline epochs (3 and 4: A=0.82+/-0.02, B=0.64+/-0.01 mas) then FIXED for the other epochs. Errors: scatter between files/exposures, 20 microarcsec for GRAVITY (formal <1 microarcsec).
flux_ratio_definition: f_B/f_A in per cent, K band; epoch average 65.4 +/- 1.6 % (epoch 1 excluded).
uncertainties: Formal fit errors are below 1 uas and the paper treats them as underestimated (data correlation, systematics). The adopted error is the scatter between the best fits of different files/exposures within an epoch: 20 uas per axis (Table 6 and Sect. 2.2). No per-epoch error ellipses are published. The paper does not mention the GRAVITY optical-aberration systematics (GRAVITY Collaboration 2021).

conventions.position: dRA, dDec = secondary B relative to primary A, east and north (as virgil's dra, ddec). PA north through east.
conventions.omega: Standard visual-orbit omega: the companion's relative to the primary, from the ascending node; the same star as virgil's omega, so no shift is applied. Checked: with this reading, crosscheck.orbits reproduces every published epoch position to better than 0.1 mas (tests/test_waisberg_references.py); the +180 deg reading is off by tens of mas.
conventions.degeneracy: Without radial velocities (Omega, omega) and (Omega + 180, omega + 180) give the same sky orbit; the paper reports the solution with Omega < 180 deg.
conventions.time: Tp is a decimal year; T_peri_mjd below = (Tp - 2000) * 365.25 + 51544.5 (Julian years), and P_day = P_yr * 365.25.

diameters_mas.source: fitted jointly in epochs 3-4; isochrone values 0.90+/-0.14 and 0.72+/-0.11 mas

third_light: No additional companion detected; K flux ratio >0.5% excluded.
notes: Single-field AT mode. Epoch 1 (2023-06-16) separation ~265 mas exceeds the AT fibre FOV (~250 mas in K): paper says very uncertain, not in flux-ratio average, flux ratio listed as 50 (fixed). Other epochs 10-46 mas, inside one fibre; NOT dual-field. Closest approach near periastron Tp=2024.526 (sep ~10 mas at epoch 4, versus 2.2 mas resolution). Fitted diameters 0.82/0.64 mas are comparable to resolution at epochs 3-4.

GRAVITY Collaboration 2021 (2021A&A...647A..59G, arXiv:2101.12098): static, field-dependent optical aberrations at fibre injection bias single-field binary astrometry (0.1-0.5 mas for S2 with the UTs in 2017-2018); dual-field pointings are not affected. These two single-field AT systems are the wide-separation cases that test whether such a bias shows in public AT data (design/gravity_aberration_test.md).
